input.content:
You are a customer service agent that helps the user.  The policy that determines how you should respond to requests from users is described below between the <policy> and </policy> tags.

In each turn you can either:
- Send a message to the user.
- Make a tool call.
You cannot do both at the same time.

<policy>
# Retail order-support policy

Use the order reference and email on the order before disclosing order details. Keep separate orders and cases separate.

For delivered-not-received packages, review carrier evidence and building checks, then open the required trace. State the carrier response deadline and make clear that a replacement is not automatic before eligibility is established. Record preferences without promising unavailable fulfillment.

For damaged items, check resolution eligibility and inventory before creating a replacement. Preserve the eligible original price. Return/no-return disposition, delivery estimate, new order reference, and notification are results of replacement creation, not separate business functions. Give safety advice for visibly wet electrical items.

For missing refunds, distinguish returned tender types. Do not issue a duplicate refund while a payment trace is open. State the review window, avoid promising bank-fee reimbursement, and attach supporting notes to the trace.
</policy>

Try to be helpful and always follow the policy.

content.text: line customer care. This is Daniel. How can I help you today?

input.content: Hi, Daniel. I'm trying to figure out what happened to a refund I asked for. I returned something at one of the stores over a week ago and the money hasn't come back yet.

content.text: Okay, I'll take a look. Was the item originally ordered online or purchased in store?

input.content: Online, and I returned it to the store. It was a black standing desk converter. It was just too wide for my desk.

content.text: Okay, got it. Do you have the order number or the return receipt nearby?

input.content: Yeah, I have both. Um, order ends in five six two four, and the return receipt ends in nine one eight two.

content.text: Okay, got it. Um, just one second. And also, what was the email address on the order?

input.content: Teddy.torrez@harbormail.com.

content.text: Okay, just give me one moment and I'm gonna look that order up.

input.content: Okay.

content.text: Okay. Um, I just found that order. I see one standing desk converter for one hundred and eighty-six dollars and forty-two cents after tax. Does that sound about right?

input.content: Yep. I paid forty dollars with a Westline gift card, and then the rest should be on my debit.

content.text: Okay, perfect. Yeah, that, that definitely helps. I can see that the return was accepted at the Eastwood store about nine days ago, and the system shows that the item is back in inventory, so the return itself is actually complete.

input.content: Oh, oh, okay. I think that's what the person at the store told me, but the email I got is only about forty-two dollars, so I'm still missing the one hundred and forty-six dollars and the forty-two cents. I don't know where that is. It isn't in my account. (concerned)

content.text: Okay, understood. Um, the, the forty dollar portion should have gone back to the gift card. Did you receive a new digital gift card number in that email by any chance?

content.text: Okay. Yeah, that's, um, that's totally fair. Let me go ahead and check the payment history and the card reference. I may need to place you on hold for a few moments while I kind of open the return details.

input.content: Yeah, sure.

content.text: Perfect. One second.

Okay. Thank you so much for waiting. Sorry about the delay. It looks like the gift card refund was issued successfully, and the debit card refund is showing submitted, um, but it was never received in like a settlement confirmation from the payment processor.

input.content: Okay. What does that mean? Did Westline send it or not? 'Cause right now my bank is saying that they don't see a refund or even something pending.

content.text: Yeah. So what that kind of means is that the store register created the refund request, but in our side, our system can't confirm that the bank accepted it. I don't want to tell you it's on the way when the status kind of says it's incomplete.

input.content: Okay.

Um, I mean, like I used a different physical card when I bought it because my card was replaced last month. It should be wired or linked to the same checking account though. Is that potentially an issue?

content.text: I will say it definitely could explain the missing confirmation. Refunds normally route to the underlying account even if a card was replaced, but sometimes the bank has to match the old card token manually. Do you remember what the last four digits of the original card were?

input.content: Yeah, um, two zero four seven. The new one ends in eight one six three.

content.text: Okay. Let me take a look to see if that's on the purchase.

Yeah. So from what I'm seeing, that does match what I see on the purchase. I'm going to open a payment trace using the original card reference, and what I'm gonna do then is attach the store return receipt. That will let our payments team confirm whether the bank rejected it or whether it's waiting on it to kind of get settled.

input.content: Um, can you just send it to the new card?

content.text: Unfortunately, not while the first refund request is still open. If I created another refund right now, you could receive both and then the system kind of blocks that. The payment team has to close or cancel the original request first.

input.content: Okay. How long does that usually take? 'Cause I returned it because I needed the money back and nine days already kind of feels like a long time.

content.text: I agree, um, that this definitely should have been cleared by now. Um, the review window is usually three to five business days from today. Many are resolved sooner, but unfortunately I just can't promise you a specific day until the processor kind of responds.

input.content: Okay. So you're saying I might be waiting another week?

content.text: Uh, potentially. Although five business days is outside the review window, if the bank confirms the accepted refund, we'll go ahead and send you the settlement reference that the bank can locate it. If the bank rejected it, Westline can reissue the amount using an approved alternative method.

input.content: Would that be a check? I don't want store credit for the whole amount, though.

content.text: It would not automatically become store credit. Depending on the processor results, the option may include the replacement card or mailed check, and the payments team will kind of confirm with you the available option before reiss-reissuing anything.

input.content: Okay. Um, can you also confirm the forty dollar gift card actually works? Like, I don't want another problem.

content.text: Yes. Um, give me one second. Let me just check that balance for you.
Yeah. So it looks like on my end that the balance and the digital gift card have forty dollars available.
It has not been used, and the number and the email, uh, still looks to be active.

input.content: Okay.

content.text: Okay. Perfect. Um, so I've kind of opened up the payment trace for the remaining a hundred and forty-six dollars and forty-two cents, and the case number is WST seven three five two oh four. And I'm also noting that your original card was actually replaced, but the checking account remains open.

input.content: Can you email that to me?

content.text: Yes. Um, I can go ahead and just send you a confirmation to your email on the order. Um, what it'll do is it should list out the amount under review, the last four digits of the original card, and then a potential expected response window.

input.content: Okay. Okay, I see it. It says not to contact the store. Does that mean that the store can't do anything right now?

content.text: Yes. So the store kind of completed, um, their part of the whole return process. From here, the payments team and the card processor have to kind of handle this. So calling the store would not kind of, uh, speed up the trace in this case.

input.content: Okay. Um, I also had a small overdraft fee because I was expecting this money back. Is that something Westline covers?

content.text: I can't approve a bank fee while the trace is open. Um, for right now, I can document it. Um, and once the refund outcome is confirmed, customer service relations can kind of review any supporting statement you choose to provide. I will say I don't want to promise any sort of reimbursement, but the note will be attached to this case.

tools.name: lookup_customer
tools.description: Find a retail customer and recent orders using a verified email or customer identifier.

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Retrieve an order with items, fulfillment, carrier scans, payments, refunds, cases, and eligible resolutions.

order_reference.description: Full or partial order reference accepted by the source system.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Retrieve product variant, price, and inventory for replacement or fulfillment decisions.

location_id.description: Optional store, pickup, or distribution location.

tools.name: open_delivery_trace
tools.description: Open a missing-package or carrier investigation with the customer's requested resolution and timing constraints.

tools.name: open_refund_trace
tools.description: Open a payment investigation for a refund that lacks settlement confirmation; do not issue a duplicate refund while it is open.

payment_reference.description: Original payment reference or masked card token.

tools.name: create_replacement_order
tools.description: Create a replacement at the eligible original price and return the new order, delivery estimate, return disposition, and notification state.

fulfillment_location.description: Address label or pickup location when known.

tools.name: update_case
tools.description: Add a note, customer preference, or supporting-information marker to an existing support case without changing its primary outcome.

tools.name: transfer_to_specialist
tools.description: Transfer the conversation with a concise reason and context summary when policy or tooling requires a specialist.

summary.description: Context already collected so the customer does not repeat it.
